extracted.intended_audience: USPTO patent examiners and patent practitioners (applicants, patent attorneys/agents)
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for determining prior art and prior-art exceptions under AIA 35 U.S.C. 102 (including 102(a)(1),(a)(2), 102(b)(1)(B), 102(b)(2)(A)/(B)/(C), and 102(d)) for patent examination and applicant submissions.

rubrics_metrics.name: AIA 35 U.S.C. 102(b)(1)(B) exception — same subject matter required
rubrics_metrics.description: What is required for subject matter in an intervening grace period disclosure to be excepted under AIA 35 U.S.C. 102(b)(1)(B) is that the same subject matter as in the intervening disclosure must have been previously publicly disclosed by the inventor or a joint inventor (or by another who obtained the subject matter therefrom).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: There is no requirement that the mode of disclosure by the inventor (patenting, publication, public use, sale) be the same as the intervening disclosure’s mode, nor that the inventor’s disclosure be verbatim. If an inventor previously disclosed A, B, and C and an intervening disclosure shows A, B, C, and D, then D remains prior art even though A–C are excepted. If an inventor disclosed a species and an intervening disclosure shows a genus (more general), the genus is excepted; conversely, a genus disclosed earlier does not except a later-disclosed species. The exception applies only to the subject matter that was previously disclosed; insubstantial or trivial differences do not defeat the exception — the subject matter must be the same.

rubrics_metrics.name: Applicant statements in specification re: inventor-originated public disclosures (37 CFR 1.77(b)(6))
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicants can include a statement in the specification upon filing regarding any inventor-originated public disclosures of subject matter made prior to a potential AIA 35 U.S.C. 102(a)(1) disclosure of that same subject matter.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: To be effective to show that a potential AIA 102(a)(1) disclosure is not prior art because 102(b)(1)(B) applies, the statement must convey the same information as required in a declaration under 37 CFR 1.130(b). Including such a reference in the specification (with an oath/declaration under 37 CFR 1.63 on file) may allow the Office to consider the exception apparent, provided there is sufficient explanation and no contrary evidence. Applicants are not required to identify such disclosures or use the 1.77(b)(6) format, but doing so may expedite examination and avoid Office actions. Applicants may not use 1.77(b)(6) to add such information after filing; instead, submit via 37 CFR 1.130(b) after filing. If the prior disclosure was a printed publication, provide a copy as required by 1.130(b).

rubrics_metrics.name: One-year grace period timing rule (extension to next business day)
rubrics_metrics.description: The one-year grace period in AIA 35 U.S.C. 102(b)(1)(B) is extended to the next succeeding business day if the end of the one-year grace period otherwise falls on a Saturday, Sunday, or federal holiday.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This extension is pursuant to 35 U.S.C. 21(b). The filing date rules under 37 CFR (e.g., 1.6(a)(2), 1.10, Priority Mail Express®, or electronic filing) still apply; the statutory extension under 35 U.S.C. 21(b) operates notwithstanding certain CFR provisions that accord filing dates for deposit/submission methods.

rubrics_metrics.name: AIA 35 U.S.C. 102(a)(2) — U.S. patent documents as prior art
rubrics_metrics.description: AIA 35 U.S.C. 102(a)(2) identifies three types of U.S. patent documents that are available as prior art as of the date they were effectively filed if they name another inventor: (1) U.S. patents; (2) U.S. patent application publications; and (3) certain WIPO published applications (treated as U.S. patent application publications).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These 'U.S. patent documents' may have different effects than under pre-AIA 102(e). A U.S. patent document may also be prior art under 102(a)(1) if its issue or publication date is before the effective filing date of the claimed invention. If the issue/publication date is not before the effective filing date, the document may still be prior art under 102(a)(2) if it was 'effectively filed' before the claimed invention’s effective filing date (see 102(d)).

rubrics_metrics.name: WIPO published PCT applications treated as U.S. publications under AIA 102(a)(2)
rubrics_metrics.description: The WIPO publication of a PCT international application designating the United States is deemed published under 35 U.S.C. 122(b) for purposes of AIA 35 U.S.C. 102(a)(2) under 35 U.S.C. 374; thus WIPO publications designating the U.S. are treated as U.S. patent application publications for prior art purposes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This treatment applies regardless of the international filing date, whether the WIPO publication is in English, or whether the PCT application later enters the U.S. national stage. Consequently, such WIPO publications that name another inventor and were effectively filed before the claimed invention’s effective filing date are prior art under 102(a)(2) unless an exception under 102(b)(2) applies.

rubrics_metrics.name: AIA 35 U.S.C. 102(d) — determining when subject matter was 'effectively filed'
rubrics_metrics.description: Under 102(d), a U.S. patent, application publication, or WIPO published application is prior art as of either its actual filing date or the filing date of a prior application to which a priority or benefit claim is made, provided that the prior-filed application 'describe[s] the subject matter' relied upon.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For 102(d) prior-art determinations the reference patent document need only meet the 'ministerial requirements' of 35 U.S.C. 119 and 120 (e.g., (1) containing a priority/benefit claim, (2) filed within the applicable period, (3) having a common inventor or same applicant). The prior-filed application must 'describe[] the subject matter' relied upon (Penumbra, Inc. v. RapidPulse, Inc.). 102(d) does not require the description to meet enablement under 35 U.S.C. 112(a). The AIA eliminated the Hilmer doctrine: if the U.S. patent document claims priority to earlier foreign/international applications that describe the subject matter, the U.S. document is effective as of the earliest such application filing date, regardless of where filed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Requirement that reference 'name another inventor' for 102(a)(2) applicability
rubrics_metrics.description: To qualify as prior art under AIA 35 U.S.C. 102(a)(2), the prior art U.S. patent document must 'name[] another inventor.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If there is any difference in inventive entity between the prior art document and the application under examination (even one joint inventor different), the prior art document satisfies the 'names another inventor' requirement. If inventors overlap, the document still qualifies as 102(a)(2) prior art unless an exception in 102(b)(2) applies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provisional rejections under 35 U.S.C. 102(a)(2) based on copending U.S. applications
rubrics_metrics.description: If an earlier-filed, copending, unpublished U.S. patent application discloses subject matter that would anticipate claims in a later-filed pending U.S. application with a different inventive entity, an examiner may determine whether a provisional rejection under 35 U.S.C. 102(a)(2) can be made.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: I. If copending applications have at least one common (joint) inventor, common applicant, or are commonly assigned, and publication/issuance of the first would qualify as 102(a)(2) prior art to the second, a provisional anticipation/obviousness rejection of the second may be made even though the first is unpublished or unissued. The provisional rejection can be overcome as any 102(a)(2) rejection can be (see MPEP §2152.06) or by abandoning and refiling a new application containing both subject matters. Use form paragraph 7.15.01.aia when making such a provisional rejection. II. If there is no common inventor/applicant/assignee and the earlier application was not published under 35 U.S.C. 122(b), maintain confidentiality and do not make a rejection relying on the earlier unpublished application; after the earlier application issues it may be used as a 102(a)(2) reference against the later application.

rubrics_metrics.name: AIA 35 U.S.C. 102(b)(2)(A) inventor-originated disclosure exception for 102(a)(2)
rubrics_metrics.description: A disclosure that would otherwise qualify as prior art under 102(a)(2) is excepted if the subject matter disclosed was obtained directly or indirectly from the inventor or a joint inventor (i.e., disclosure by another who obtained the subject matter from the inventor/joint inventor).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants may establish entitlement to the exception by affidavit or declaration of attribution under 37 CFR 1.130(a). Applicants can include a statement in the specification at filing per 37 CFR 1.77(b)(6) to identify inventor-originated disclosures in U.S. patent documents; such a statement must convey the same information as required in a 1.130(a) declaration to be effective. Including the information in the specification (with an oath/declaration under 1.63) may make the exception apparent, but applicants may not add such information to the specification after filing via 1.77(b)(6); use 1.130(a) after filing.

rubrics_metrics.name: AIA 35 U.S.C. 102(b)(2)(B) inventor-originated prior public disclosure exception for 102(a)(2)
rubrics_metrics.description: A disclosure that would otherwise qualify as prior art under 102(a)(2) (a U.S. patent document) is excepted if the subject matter disclosed had been previously publicly disclosed by the inventor, a joint inventor, or another who obtained the subject matter directly or indirectly from the inventor or joint inventor.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: There is no requirement that the mode of prior disclosure by the inventor match the mode of the intervening U.S. patent document, nor that it be verbatim. The subject matter in the intervening reference relied upon must be the same subject matter previously publicly disclosed by the inventor (mere insubstantial or trivial/obvious variations do not satisfy the 'same subject matter' requirement). The exception applies only to those parts of the intervening U.S. patent document that were previously publicly disclosed; other new subject matter in the intervening document remains available as prior art. Examples: inventor disclosed species and intervening document discloses genus — genus excepted; inventor disclosed genus and intervening document discloses species — species available as prior art. To be effective, applicant statements in the specification must convey the same information as a declaration under 37 CFR 1.130(b); applicants may submit affidavits/declarations under 1.130(b) to show prior public disclosure by the inventor/joint inventor.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prior-art exceptions under AIA 35 U.S.C. 102(b)(2) categories
rubrics_metrics.description: AIA 35 U.S.C. 102(b)(2) contains multiple exceptions to prior art under 102(a)(2): (A) inventor-originated disclosure exception; (B) inventor-originated prior public disclosure exception; and (C) common ownership or obligation of assignment exception.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: MPEP §2154.02(a) discusses 102(b)(2)(A), §2154.02(b) discusses 102(b)(2)(B), and §2154.02(c) discusses 102(b)(2)(C). Each exception may apply regardless of the potential prior-art date under 102(a)(2) (i.e., no grace-period limitation); factual showing (affidavit/declaration) may be required to establish applicability.
